justification: Two new DQ ledger rows with checks (freeze rule), and a guard in a registry-writing script. No serving code, no schema, no production write in this PR.

pre_impl.existing_data: Reused dq_probe_app_defects.py (_sql_count, _db) and its real-DB test file; the guard reads lga_registry.parent_lga, the rollup the project rules name. DQ-105's note already describes these 11 rows, but as a false positive in its own check, not as a defect -- no existing check counts them.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The prompt said 'find what writes inner_west'. Measured: dcp_extract_changed.py copies dcp_chapter_registry.council; the wrong value came from register_orphan_chapters.py NEW_CHAPTERS (registry ids 747-749). All three duplicate chapters already registered under the former council, and no current dcp_setback_controls row references them.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Additive: two ledger rows, two probe functions, one guard. Three NEW_CHAPTERS tuples removed so a rerun cannot re-register the duplicates.
pre_impl.external_source_error: N/A -- no external source; the checks read the production DB (exit 2 when unreachable) and a source file.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: None from this PR. The defect it logs: a Marrickville or Ashfield property is served duplicate and page-footer text as rules (DQ-128), and the public page calls a former-council plan a council (DQ-129).

falsifiable_check.command: python scripts/dq_probe_app_defects.py --id DQ-128 ; python scripts/dq_probe_app_defects.py --id DQ-129 ; python scripts/dq_check.py --coverage
falsifiable_check.fails_when: DQ-128 exits 1 while any served row carries a parent slug on a former council's document; DQ-129 exits 1 while the stat says 'councils' and the list names a former council.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Both exit 1 on production today (11 rows; 'councils' with leichhardt). dq_check --id for each PASSES because both are declared open. Unit tests force each outcome (red, clean, could-not-look).

functions.name: dq128
functions.input: no arguments; reads regulatory_provisions joined to lga_registry on production

functions.name: dq129
functions.input: page.tsx text, dcp-scoped-councils.json, lga_registry former councils
functions.output: 1 when the stat unit is 'councils' and a former council is listed; 1 when the stat no longer reads the list
functions.if_none: no former councils or none listed -> 0; DB unreachable -> 2

functions.name: former_council_owner
functions.input: a dict cursor, the merged council's slug, and the plan's dcp_name
functions.output: former council slug when dcp_name begins with a former council's display name followed by a space; else None

break_it.scenario: Someone reruns register_orphan_chapters.py after the 11 rows are retired.
break_it.what_happens: The three Inner West duplicates would be re-registered and re-extracted under the wrong slug.
break_it.how: Tuples removed; test_no_inner_west_former_council_chapter_is_listed_for_registration; and the guard refuses any future such tuple (real-DB test against lga_registry).

break_it.scenario: A former council display name is a prefix of an unrelated plan name.
break_it.what_happens: A legitimate plan would be refused registration under its own council.
break_it.how: Match requires the display name followed by a space; test_a_name_that_only_starts_with_the_same_letters_is_not_refused.

break_it.scenario: DQ-129 is cleared by hardcoding the stat text instead of fixing the unit.
break_it.what_happens: The count could drift from the list and the check would go silent.
break_it.how: dq129 returns 1 when the stat no longer reads scopedCouncils.councils.length (test_dq129_red_when_the_stat_stops_reading_the_list).

post_merge.db_reset: No. The production retirement of the 16 current rows and registry 747-749 is a separate, backed-up write that needs the user's go.
post_merge.manual_verify: After the write: dq_probe_app_defects --id DQ-128 exits 0, then flip DQ-128 to fixed in a small PR.
